newsitem.title: ITALY: De Benedetti warns on jobs at Olivetti.
newsitem.headline: De Benedetti warns on jobs at Olivetti.

text.p: Carlo De Benedetti, ex-chairman of struggling Italian hi-tech group Olivetti, on Thursday warned of the worsening crisis at the loss-making company which threatens the jobs of the group's 28,000-strong workforce.

De Benedetti's comments to a parliamentary committee came a day after Olivetti's chief executive Roberto Colaninno said its recovery plan to sell-off some divisions may have to be delayed and that a parliamentary inquiry would force the group to close.
"The climate that has been created around Olivetti is perhaps the most serious threat weighing on thousands," he told the lower house parliamentary committee.

De Benedetti, who headed the group for nearly 20 years until his resignation in September, said he supported Colaninno's recovery plan of focusing on computer systems and telecoms and selling-off other divisions to cut the group's heavy debt level.

He stressed that Olivetti had financial problems but it had a range of technology and skills that was rare in the country, and was confident that the group could transform itself into a true information technology group.

De Benedetti first bought into Olivetti, based in the Italian northwestern town of Ivrea, through his family holding company CIR and is Olivetti's largest shareholder with around 15 percent stake. He is still honourary president of Olivetti.

Colaninno's comments on Wednesday to the same committee caused the shares to weaken on Thursday. He said plans to sell-off its loss-making personal computer company by the end of this year may be delayed, while the sale of its profitable speciality computer group Tecnost could be reviewed.
Olivetti shares were off 3.11 percent at 530 lire in a slightly firmer Milan bourse at 1330 GMT, while Tecnost shares were suspended by the stock exchange after a sharp fall.

After Olivetti sold a stake in mobile phone consortium Omnitel last month for 432.5 billion lire ($286 million), it was hoped the sale of the PC business and of Tecnost would raise enough cash for Olivetti to meet an 800 billion lire sell-off target for 1996.
Colaninno plans more sell-offs to raise 400 billion lire in 1997, largely from the partial float of office equipment company Lexikon, which it is hoped will bring Olivetti's hugh debt under control.
The group will then consider a rights issue to re-finance the company for future growth.
On Wednesday, Colaninno also warned that if an official parliamentary Olivetti inquiry was launched, the company would lose its customers overnight and could be forced to close.

Olivetti is already under investigation by prosecutors and stock market authority Consob after the group's director general in charge of finance and auditing Renzo Francesconi resigned saying first half 1996 results underestimated losses and debts. ($1=1,510 lire)
